title: Ring segmentation at scan scale: draw rings, split regions and cut parts out on a full crawfish scan
description: Every check of the ring tool, region tool and region extraction so far ran on fertility (~15k vertices) and small test tubes. A crawfish scan is ~623k vertices / ~936k triangles. Run the whole segmentation flow on one repaired scan (ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/crawfish_repaired.dsl, IMG_4109.glb through repair_mesh) in the ring-tool scene: activate the ring tool, hover-preview and draw rings around one claw, one walking leg and the tail, confirm and save them (into a tmp/ copy of the dsl), Ctrl+T to split regions, pick each part and E to cut it out as its own closed mesh. Record wall time and peak heap for every step: scene load, ring-tool activation (limb-axis skeleton, intrinsic triangulation), hover preview latency (GirdlingPlane.find has had its length cap removed in CRAW-40, so measure it here), ring trace/tighten, region split, extraction. Anything that is too slow to use interactively (target: hover preview under ~50 ms, activation and region split in seconds) or runs out of memory is fixed here if small, otherwise written up as its own ticket with the profile. Not decimation: the scan is not degraded to make it fit (same ruling as CRAW-2). Profile with run-scene --profile and ixdar_automation_cli.async_profile. Exported meshes are not needed; seeing the segments in the scene is the goal.
definition-of-done: 1. On the full repaired scan, rings around a claw, a leg and the tail are drawn, saved, reloaded, split into regions and each part cut out closed (Manifold NO_ERROR), with screenshots under tmp/. 2. A timing and heap table per step is on the ticket; every step meets the interactive targets or has a filed follow-up ticket with its profile. 3. fertility_rings.dsl is never saved over; its 13 ring fingerprints are unchanged by any fix made here.
testing-plan: 1. Drive the flow with ixdar-cli (launch, hover, click, key, ui-state) on a tmp/ copy of crawfish_repaired.dsl, logging per-step timings and heap. 2. Profile the slowest step with run-scene --profile. 3. Re-check fertility fingerprints after any fix.
changes-made:
Full flow run on crawfish_repaired.dsl (IMG_4109 through repair_mesh: 469,131 vertices / 938,302 triangles after repair) in ring-tool, on tmp/crawfish_rings.dsl. Rings: claw (ring_00, 266 edges, fingerprint 2e825ad314260fe0), walking leg (ring_01, 79 edges, 8276d8d8dbdccaf8), tail fan (ring_03, 325 edges, 3f51890db2075257); saved, relaunched, all three reload with the same fingerprints; Ctrl+T splits 10 regions with no problems; E extracts claw (130,536 faces), leg (14,718) and tail fan (40,684), each closed=true, manifold NO_ERROR. Wall time is the logged in-scene time (round trip of the automation call in brackets); peak heap is jstat used heap sampled every 50 ms (DSL nodes: the graph's own per-node peak). Default max heap, no OOM.

Profile of body hovers (tmp/profile-hover.html): GirdlingPlane.find is ~16% of RingTool.previewAt (9 of 58 samples); the rest is the spline fit (SurfaceSplineTracer.subdivide / retraceSegment, SurfaceGeodesics.geodesic). Filed CRAW-43.
Fixed: (1) ModelCatalog.packagedGraph took every -Dixdar.mesh.dsl value as a name below src/main/resources/dsl, so an absolute path resolved to src/main/resources/dsl/<abs path>, found no file and fell back to loading a classpath resource of that name, which fails: the scene could not open a tmp/ copy. An absolute path is now the graph's own file, read and saved in place. (2) ConformingLoopSnap pruned dead-end spurs only on polygon meshes, but on the fine triangle scan consecutive traced points snap to vertices A, B, A, the walk marks edge AB once and leaves a spur; RingRegions then saw a loose end and refused the leg and tail rings ("open: 1 loose end(s); it walls nothing"). Spurs are now pruned on every closed path; unit test ConformingLoopSnapTest. fertility_rings.dsl's 13 ring fingerprints are identical before and after (loaded read-only).
Observations, not filed: the leg ringed is its own shell in the repaired scan (15,120 faces, disconnected from the body); this scan's abdomen is curled under the carapace, so the tail ring cuts the tail fan; the claw extraction capped 3 boundary loops for a region bounded by one ring (still closed, NO_ERROR).

User's own crawfish segmentation (12 rings, 5-12 authored anchors each, saved 2026-10-03 21:55 into the worktree's tmp/crawfish_rings.dsl) promoted to the tracked fixture ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl (md5 b9d40a96...), with a kept launch entry 'Ring Tool (crawfish)' (-Dixdar.mesh.dsl=fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl). Note: this agent's own rings were single-click girdle cuts, not anatomical boundaries; the brief asked only for timings and closed extraction. Treat CRAW-41 as a scale test, not a segmentation.
